C1_skipped_autowired.note: Verified at TelegramApiClient.java:45-51 — class has two constructors (public 2-arg with @Value, package-private 3-arg test seam). Spring 4.3's single-constructor auto-detection requires exactly one constructor; with two, an @Autowired marker is needed to disambiguate the injection target. Removing @Autowired would cause Spring to fail bean construction. Skip is technically correct. The codebase comparison to EmailService.java cited in round-1 C1 does not apply — EmailService has a single constructor.

considered_but_dismissed.candidate: requireValidTokenShape throws IllegalArgumentException synchronously, breaking reactive composition
considered_but_dismissed.reasoning: Intentional fail-fast defense-in-depth. Upstream @Pattern bean-validation is the primary boundary; this is a secondary programmer-error guard that should never fire in production. IllegalArgumentException flows to GlobalErrorHandler's Throwable handler (500 generic). Wrapping in Mono.defer would obscure the programmer-error nature. Acceptable trade-off.

considered_but_dismissed.candidate: mapClientError onErrorResume silently swallows body-read errors without DEBUG logging
considered_but_dismissed.reasoning: Triggered only on 4xx where the operator-actionable info is the HTTP status, not the body. Status is logged via toAppException's warn line at line 140 with rawStatus context. No diagnostic loss for the documented failure modes (non-JSON body, empty body).

considered_but_dismissed.candidate: MONO_TIMEOUT (10s) duplicates DEFAULT_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT (10s) as separate constants
considered_but_dismissed.reasoning: They serve different layers: DEFAULT_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT is Reactor Netty's per-response timeout (lower-level); MONO_TIMEOUT is the operator-level safety net for cases where Netty's timeout doesn't fire (e.g., body never completes after headers). Same value today, but conceptually independent — separation is intentional per tech-spec edge-case note.
